title: Powers
summary: Choose a power set around the role you want to play.

sections.title: How powers work
items: Choose your power set during character creation. Active powers unlock as you level; all active powers in your set are available at level 30.
Every power set supports the Damage role. Each also has a support role: Tank, Controller, or Healer.

sections.title: Tank power sets
items: Fire, Ice, Earth, Rage, and Atomic support tanking. Tanks attract enemy attention and absorb attacks to protect the group.

sections.title: Controller power sets
items: Gadgets, Mental, Light, Quantum, and Munitions support controlling. Controllers supply group power and incapacitate enemies.

sections.title: Healer power sets
items: Sorcery, Nature, Electricity, Celestial, and Water support healing. Healers restore the health of their teammates.

sections.title: Starting choices
items: Fire, Gadgets, Ice, Mental, Nature, and Sorcery are the classic character-creation power sets. Check current in-game access before purchasing additional powers.

sections.title: Roles, stats and additional powers
items: Tanks emphasize Defense, Health and Dominance, draw enemy attention, absorb attacks and provide group immunity to control effects.
Controllers emphasize Vitalization and Dominance, restore group Power and incapacitate enemies. Healers emphasize Restoration and Power to restore group Health.
All power sets can play Damage, emphasizing Precision and Might to defeat enemies and complete objectives.
Spend stat points in the movement-mode tree or Iconic Powers to gain additional active abilities.

sections.title: Complexity
items: Character Creation, as of 2025, classifies Powers by their complexity to use:
Simple: Fire, Munitions, Electricity
Standard: Sorcery, Mental, Ice, Quantum
High: Gadgets, Nature, Earth, Light, Water
Very High: Celestial, Rage, Atomic

sections.title: Atomic
items: Utilize the power of nuclear energy, rearranging the atomic structure of yourself, your allies, and your enemies at will. Split Atoms, cause Thermochemical Explosions, and burn under the intense Nuclear Pressure causing unreal destruction. Transmute into fortified metal and reorganize your atomic structure to protect you and your allies or harness the power of the building blocks of all matter to lay waste to your enemies. Explode with harmful radiation, reducing your enemies to ash and speeding up your recovery. Manipulate the subatomic structure of enemies to shield you and your allies.

sections.title: Celestial
items:
Keep your allies alive with cleansing Holy Magic or Dark Unholy rituals. Characters using Celestial Powers can shape the forces of the universe, Bless their allies and/or Curse their enemies. Wield divine powers to restrain and overwhelm your enemies and to soothe the wounds of your allies.
Command dark powers to restrain and overwhelm your enemies and to mend the wounds of your allies.

sections.title: Earth
items: Characters that choose earth will rumble on to the scene and shake things up. Earth Powers can be used for both Tanking and Damage and features a Tanking mechanic that defers damage to a player's summoned Golem. Shape Earthen constructs to crush enemies and reinforce allies. Call mighty, Earth-shaking forces to rattle and daze opponents.

sections.title: Electricity
items: Characters that choose electricity will imbue themselves with lightning. Electricity characters use these powers to shock their enemies or revitalize allies. They also want to spread their electricity so they can do as much damage to groups as possible. Electrify your enemies and resuscitate your allies. Manipulate and damage enemies with electrostatic forces.

sections.title: Fire
items:
Players who choose to wield the wild and unpredictable forces of fire have to be tough. Fire characters like to get up front and blast away at enemies, and therefore they tend to draw a lot of attention. Cause flames to well up around your character, causing damage to anyone in the vicinity.
Flames burst forth, searing your opponents and their nearby allies.

sections.title: Gadgets
items: Characters with the gadget power will find themselves pulling out all manner of devices from their pockets and pouches. On the front lines, a well-placed gadget will help you control not only the enemy but the battlefield itself. Gadget characters are crafty and use their heads to place their devices strategically to achieve victory. Slip through the shadows and deploy cunning gadgets to manipulate the battlefield. Employ a variety of devious and deadly contraptions to baffle your foes.

sections.title: Ice
items: Characters that choose to master subzero temperatures make for challenging foes. During combat, ice wielders have the ability to lock down opponents who come within their chilling reach. Ice forms around you and enemy attacks don't seem to land. By using your powers to create defenses for yourself, you are a master of mitigating damage. When the occasional attack does strike true, the cold is passed on to your attacker, often freezing them in their tracks. Icy winds dance at your command, allowing you to push and pull enemies around the battlefield. No one can escape your arctic blasts, which allows you to control the direction of the fight.

sections.title: Light
items: The rings that grant the ability to create Hard Light Constructs are given to only a chosen few. In times of great crisis, however, the Green Lantern and Sinestro Corps may choose individuals to be reservists, thereby swelling the ranks of Light Powered heroes and villains. Those who wield the power of Light are ideal front-line combatants dealing massive damage with imaginative constructs, or supporting their allies when the fight gets thickest. Heroes wield the green power of Will, while Villains use the yellow power of Fear. Light characters can chain deadly and devastating combinations called Construct Combos by using a power followed by certain weapon combos. A Light powered warrior is tough to defeat when charging in to battle with deadly constructs. Rain devastation on your enemies with missiles and bombs, blast them with a hail of bullets, or smash them out of the way with brute force. In the midst of a tough group battle the power of Light can be used to support the team in many ways. Throttle and stun an enemy with a giant hand or use a blast of light to recharge your team's power.

sections.title: Mental
items: Characters with the mental superpower are masters of mind over matter. Using their unique abilities, they can move objects with a thought to defend themselves or damage an enemy. They can also use the force of their will in more subtle ways, such as creating illusions to disorient and confuse. Mental characters love to be where the action is and control the battlefield with their minds. With the brute force of your will, you can create force fields that encase enemies or send them flying down the street. By using your mental powers, create opportunities for surprise attacks. Such power can even make an opponent think they see something that isn't there.

sections.title: Munitions
items:
Lock, load, and become a master of explosives and ballistics. Run and gun as you cut paths of destruction through your enemies with big guns and bigger explosions. Use your ordnance expertise to take control on the battlefield or simply blast right through the fray. Lay waste to the battlefield and any enemies that happen to be there with military-grade ordnance.
Knowledge of up-and-coming prototype artillery is half of the battle.

sections.title: Nature
items:
Characters that choose the nature power will find themselves masters over primal forces. Nature characters draw upon these forces to keep their allies alive or wither their enemies away. When the battle gets really tough, they can also let the call of the wild surge through them and actually become a beast full of rage, cunning and animal instincts. Wield poisonous botanical powers to restrain and overwhelm your enemies and to soothe the wounds of allies.
Call forth the attributes of a variety of frightening and fantastic animals to dominate enemies and aid allies.

sections.title: Quantum
items: Manipulate time, control gravity and twist the very fabric of space itself! Characters using Quantum Powers can slow down opponents, change their density, or even teleport behind them by altering time, manipulating gravity, and folding space. Control the flow of time and control your enemies futures. Bring your enemies to their knees by manipulating space and generating graviton fields.

sections.title: Rage
items: Tap into the Rage of the emotional spectrum to create energy blasts, deadly blood plasma attacks, and even vicious constructs. Wield this Red Light with righteous fury or be driven by vengeance and petty anger. Anger powers allow you to eradicate your enemies through blind rage. Defer incoming damage and share your rage with your allies.

sections.title: Sorcery
items:
Characters who wield the unseen forces of the universe hold the power of life and death in their hands. Sorcerers can doom enemies to failure or ensure their allies have the power to carry on the fight. They are ideal for combat support, often tipping the balance of a fight with their spells.
Drawn to your mystical power, fantastic arcane creatures never leave your side. Choose wisely which pet you summon, for each will behave according to the mystic forces that created it. Whether attacking, defending, or performing some other fantastic feat, legions of powerful minions are at your service. The fate of many rests in your hands as you change the course of battle. Generate good or bad karma for you, your allies, or foes. Gathering these positive and negative energies allows you to elevate or enfeeble those around you.

sections.title: Water
items: Keep your allies alive with powerful storms and flowing water. Command water in and around allies and enemies. Bend and blast water into incredible streams and torrents to unleash a flood of destruction, or shape it into awe-inspiring constructs to wash away your enemies. Soothe the wounds of your allies or envelop them and yourself with the shielding power of water. And turn the tides of conflicts by pulling strength from the mystical energies of the ocean depths.

sections.title: Iconic Powers
items: Iconic Powers are special powers, which are uniquely associated with specific DC Universe characters. Examples of iconic powers are Heat Vision, Word of Power, and Neo-Venom Boost, which are associated with Superman, Shazam, and Bane, respectively. All characters can purchase iconic powers, regardless of the power set they chose at character creation.

sections.title: Artifact Powers
items: Certain artifacts grant access to new powers. Examples of such artifacts are The Omega Totality, M.E.R.C.Y. Amazotron Matrix, B.O.P. Commlink, Brand of Hecate and Source Shard. Artifact powers become available once the artifact is at least rank 80.

sections.title: Notes
items: All powers activated from the power tray and their combos cause damage based on Might.
Most powers support Power Interactions.
Character's main power set will affect the color as well as some other visual effects of weapon attacks. One of the most noticeable examples is Martial Arts' Spinning Punch combo.
Certain Allies and Artifacts can modify effects of powers.
Certain powers can be cast faster than their animation by use of Clipping.
Certain powers can be canceled early, for example finishers by pressing the jump button.
On March 31st, 2015, previous DLC packs were separated into Episodes, Powers, Upgrades and Legends characters.

Before game update 73 Power points could be reset and altered in-game through the use of the R.A.D. Kiosk, located in the Aquacultural area of the JLA Watchtower, or the B.A.D. Kiosk located in The Pit of the Hall of Doom. Now these devices are only used to reset skill points.

title: Grab and Smash
summary: Retrieve five pieces of information inside the Cape Carmine Lighthouse duo.

sections.title: Before entering
items: The source identifies Arcane Edict #020 as the hero unlock. Its villain edict number is unspecified.
Track the mission in your Journal before queuing for Cape Carmine Lighthouse through On Duty. The source warns that the walk-in version does not work.

sections.title: Terminal route
items: After the Venom Supplier Diego fight, go through the door and look to the left.
Look in the room where you fight Killer Croc or Huntress.
Check the lobby for the Killer Croc and Deathstroke, or Huntress and Nightwing, fight.
Check the western side of the corridor leading to Bane.
Find the final terminal in the corridor leading to the exit.

sections.title: Rewards
items: The source lists 1,162 cash and a Source Mark. These values have not been verified in the current game.

sections.title: Mission objective and terminal views
items: Bane's street soldiers are trading information about increased magical activity in Gotham. Retrieve five pieces of information before the gang can profit from it.

Interact with all five terminals during the queued duo. If a terminal is not interactive, confirm this mission was tracked in the Journal before starting the run. The pictures below correspond to the five numbered map screenshots in Location & maps.

sections.title: Which version are you entering?

sections.title: Inside the lighthouse
items: Bane and his Venom-powered gang occupy the lighthouse. Nightwing and Killer Croc pursue Bane and his Venom supply.

title: Feats
summary: Earn feat points, gain skill points, and understand optional unlocks for alternate characters.

sections.title: Earning skill points
items: Feats reward completion of challenges across exploration, solo content, group instances, PvP, and other activities. Every 100 feat points grants one additional skill point, allowing progression beyond the points gained through leveling.

sections.title: Star ratings and points
items: Read the requirement of each feat before attempting it. Four-star feats are special rewards and do not necessarily demand more effort than three-star challenges.

sections.title: Unlocking feats on another character
items: Replay badges can grant eligible feats already earned by another character. This is optional: feats can still be earned by completing their normal requirements. Only feats shared by the characters are eligible, so movement-specific feats cannot be transferred to an incompatible movement type.

The source lists badge costs of 1, 3, 5, and 7 for feats worth 10, 25, 50, and 100 points respectively. Check the in-game unlock confirmation before spending badges. Some event-progression feats can instead be obtained on other characters by reclaiming their associated rewards.

sections.title: Finding your next goal
items: Use the feats menu to inspect requirements and progress. A yellow ribbon marks feats that also award a title. The menu was reorganized in Game Update 135; older screenshots and navigation instructions may differ from the current interface.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Feats Icon
One of the many features in DC Universe Online is the Feats section. Feats are self-contained challenges that award points upon completion.
Challenge Dynamo

DC Universe Online feats contain challenges covering every aspect of gameplay, including Exploration, Alerts, Raids and PvP. More feats will be added as new content becomes available in game, so additional feats can be expected on a regular basis.

sections.title: Feats Menu
items: The feats menu can be accessed by pressing the escape key, then clicking on the trophy icon at the bottom of the screen. This will bring up a list of options, the first option is feats.
Feats Menu
The feats menu is split into 3 sections: Categories, Recent Accomplishments and Progress Overview.
Categories section shows a list of subcategories for feats e.g. Exploration, Alerts, Solo Content and PVP.
Recent Accomplishments section shows the last 3 feats you completed.
Progress Overview section shows the total number of feats available in each subcategory and how many you have completed.
Feat providing a Title
Feats which grant titles are denoted by a yellow ribbon in the feats menu.
The game's original feats menu was completely reorganized with game update 135.

items: For every 100 points achieved the player will receive an additional skill point for their character. Completing feats will allow you to gain new skill points beyond what you can achieve through leveling alone.
The number of points awarded for completing each feat varies based on difficulty, easy feats award 10 points whereas the most difficult/time consuming award 50 points.

sections.title: Difficulty Rating/Points Awarded
items: Each feat has a star rating, which reflects the difficulty of accomplishing that feat. The star rating also indicates how many points you receive upon completion.
4 Star feats are generally not "hard to achieve" per se - there are plenty of 3 Star feats vastly more challenging or grindy - but most recently seemingly exclusive to limited-time special events.

Since game update 34 feats the player has achieved with another character can be unlocked with replay badges.

sections.title: Notes
items: 1 skill point is achieved every 100 feat points, thus you need to spend 100-120 replay badges to level up a character 10 skill points and 1000-1200 replay badges to level up a character 100 skill points .

Its not necessary to use replay badges, instead they are a way to speed up skill point progression by effectively buying feats that you've already obtained on another character. However, those feats you could buy with replay badges are still obtainable as normal. Some new players might assume that you must unlock the feats obtained with another character before you can obtain them on another, this is a misconception brought about by the term "unlock". Unlocking merely grants you the feat without going about the normal means of obtaining it.

More recent 100 points feats, achieved via the event progression system, can be achieved on other player characters by reclaiming their related rewards and thus don't need to be unlocked with replay badges.

title: Equipment
summary: Understand weapons, costume pieces, and the other items your character carries.

sections.title: Choosing weapons
items: Your weapon type determines the attacks and combos available in combat. Weapon types offer different combinations of ranged and melee attacks. Characters can develop more than one weapon type; choose based on the attacks you want to use and your combat role.

sections.title: Costume equipment
items: Costume pieces contribute character statistics. Role and character-level requirements can restrict which pieces you can equip. Compare usable equipment separately from its visual style when choosing upgrades.

sections.title: Other item types
items: Inventory items serve several purposes beyond equipped armor and weapons. Trinkets and consumables can assist in combat, collection items contribute to sets, and base items provide decoration. Currency and crafting materials have separate progression uses.

sections.title: Weapon types
items: The source lists Bow, Brawling, Dual Pistols, Dual Wield, Hand Blaster, Martial Arts, One-Handed, Rifle, Shield, Staff, and Two-Handed. For cross-weapon combos, see the Weapon Mastery guide. Check current in-game access requirements for restricted weapon types.

title: Weapon Mastery
summary: Unlock stronger weapon combos and chain attacks into another weapon type.

sections.title: Unlocking mastery
items: Weapon Mastery becomes available after spending the required stat points in a weapon tree. Unlocking mastery for your equipped weapon increases damage from its weapon combos. Check the tree in game for the exact point requirements.

sections.title: Multiple Mastery
items: Cross-weapon combos require the corresponding mastery unlocks in the other weapon trees. You do not need to own a secondary weapon item to perform its unlocked mastery combo. Unlocking the combo also adds an appearance option in the Style UI.

sections.title: Combo reference
items: Each row lists the secondary weapon trees and the four combo sequences recorded by the source. The first two sequences are labeled melee and the last two ranged in that reference. These are source-listed sequences, not independently tested damage rankings.

sections.title: Practice and appearance
items: The source notes that mastery combos can be performed without hitting an enemy or sparring target. Secondary and tertiary weapon appearances can be selected in the style menu, including a default energy-construct appearance using the primary character color.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Original WM Animation
Weapon Mastery is a system available to all players. It was introduced with the Amazon Fury Part I episode.

sections.title: Overview
items: Weapon Mastery requires a specific number of Stat Points spent in a Weapon Tree to unlock. The player gains increased damage when using weapon combos if Weapon Mastery is unlocked for the equipped weapon type.
Multiple Mastery allows combos into other Weapons if Weapon Mastery is unlocked in other Weapon trees.
Unlocking a Multiple Mastery combo will also add an appearance option for that weapon in the Style UI.
While you need the type and the mastery unlocked, you do not need to own the secondary weapon in order to complete the mastery combo.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Previously, in order to successfully exercise Weapon Mastery, the player needed to focus on an enemy or a Sparring Target. This has since been changed and you can perform the combos without hitting anything.

It is possible to set the weapon styles for the secondary and tertiary weapon via the style menu. There is a unique "Default" style for secondary and tertiary weapons that looks like a simple energy construct in the player's primary colour.

Neither Staff nor Shield appear in any other weapon tree's Mastery list. While Shield's exclusion is understandable due to being a fighting style only available with a purchase, Staff's exclusion is odd and unexplained. title: Artifacts
summary: Equip long-term upgrades and improve them with Nth Metal and catalyst breakthroughs.

sections.title: Equipping artifacts
items: Artifacts use dedicated equipment slots. Each artifact type can be equipped only once, so duplicate copies cannot fill multiple slots. Unlike frequently replaced combat-rating gear, artifacts develop through a longer-term investment in ranks.

sections.title: Obtaining your first artifact
items: The source describes an introductory Artifacts mission from John Constantine, available at level 20. After completing it, additional artifacts can be obtained from Constantine in the House of Legends, Watchtower, or Hall of Doom. Individual artifacts may also come from mission rewards, Time Capsules, or grants. Check the vendor and the specific artifact source before spending currency.

sections.title: Fortifying and breakthroughs
items: Use Nth Metal to add item experience through the artifact fortification interface. Higher-quality Nth Metal provides more experience. Gaining enough experience increases the artifact rank and its statistical bonuses.

Every 20 ranks is a milestone requiring specific catalysts for a breakthrough. The source identifies John Constantine and certain episode vendors as catalyst sources. Inspect the breakthrough requirements for your current artifact rather than assuming every milestone uses the same catalyst combination.

sections.title: Choosing an artifact
items: Artifacts can provide passive or active abilities as well as statistics. Match those effects to the role and play style you want to support. The available effects depend on the artifact and its rank; this overview does not supply unverified item-level statistics.

sections.title: Source consistency note
items: The source introduction still describes three artifact slots, while its update history records five slots from game update 155. The reproduced source overview below is historical in that respect; consult the current in-game inventory for slot availability.

sections.title: Source overview
items: An Artifact is a new type of gear equipped in three Artifact slots, and that you can rank up and fortify with Nth metal to unlock powerful bonuses. Unlike other types of gear that you replace frequently as you advance in combat rating, Artifacts require a long term investment and grow with your character. Many Artifacts will also grant new passive or active abilities starting from rank 80 to 200 in addition to stats, and will provide new options for how you build or play your character.
Each type of artifact can only be equipped once, it is not possible to equip two or three of the same artifact type at the same time.

sections.title: Obtaining Artifacts
items: You will get your first Artifact by completing the Artifacts Mission from John Constantine (available at level 20). Once completed, you can obtain additional Artifacts from Constantine in the House of Legends, Watchtower or Hall of Doom for 10 Source Marks.
Some artifacts are also available via mission rewards, Time Capsules, or the Grant system, although they are usually also available from Constantine for 10 Source Marks.

sections.title: Upgrading Artifacts
items: In your inventory, there is a new tab called Artifacts. Once you have an Artifact and some Nth Metal, you can combine the two to add Item Experience to the Artifact. Different kinds of Nth Metal are worth different amounts of Item Experience. Get enough Item Experience into your Artifact and it will increase in Rank. Each Rank gives a small, exponentially increasing stat boost. Every 20 Ranks is a Milestone Rank, which offers larger bonuses and requires specific Catalysts to breakthrough.

sections.title: Reagents
items: Nth Metal is the core reagent for your Artifact. Once you’ve acquired your first Artifact, you’ll be able to find Nth Metal as a rare drop from defeating NPCs. In addition, you’ll be able to get large caches of Nth Metal by completing the Vault and Stabilizer Fragmentation. Nth Metal comes in various qualities, with rarer, more refined pieces granting larger amounts of Item Experience when used to fortify your Artifact.
Sin Stones are another reagent for Artifacts. They are only available from Assassin Time Capsules.
Sunstones are yet another reagent for Artifacts. They are only available from Kryptonian Time Capsules.
Artifacts that players no longer wish to possess can be used as reagents to level up other artifacts. However less than half of the XP contained will be recycled.
Container Artifacts usually have their own special reagents.

sections.title: Catalysts
items: Catalysts are special items required to break through Milestone Ranks. These can be acquired from John Constantine and certain episode vendors. Each Milestone Rank requires a different and specific combination of Catalysts.

sections.title: Feats
items: Various feats are available related to artifacts.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Artifacts will be temporarily disabled in PvP instances.
Artifacts were introduced with game update 76.
With hotfix 18/01/18 a second artifact slot was introduced making it possible to equip two different artifacts at the same time.
With hotfix 15/02/18 the maximum rank of artifacts was increased from 100 to 120.
With game update 84 the maximum rank of artifacts was increased from 120 to 160.
With game update 86 a third artifact slot was introduced making it possible to equip three different artifacts at the same time.
With game update 97 the maximum rank of artifacts was increased from 160 to 200.
With game update 155 a fourth and fifth artifact slot was introduced making it possible to equip five different artifacts at the same time.

Usually milestone rank 80 is at 39,920 experience, rank 100 at 82,499 experience, rank 120 at 167,659 experience, rank 140 at 337,979 experience, rank 160 at 678,722 experience, rank 180 at 1,178,722 experience and rank 200 is at 1,678,722 experience. The best freely available reagent yields 3,000 XP and is available as a bonus from Doctor Fate's Daily Rewards.

title: The Precipice of Fear
summary: Find all six of Dr. Crane's research notes around the East End and Gotham Sewer.

sections.title: Part 1: Fear Itself
items: On the top of a building under construction right in front of the East End Police Station, behind a Box Pallet.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 905: Roosevelt said: 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.' He was, of course, utterly wrong."

sections.title: Part 2: Anxiety's Sting
items: There are two nodes for this part. One is located just Southwest of the East End Bowery point in the map (behind the fence), while the other is two blocks West from the Bowery, under the railway to the North.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 910: To acquaint the nervousness of a first date, with the sheer terror one must feel in a plane crash, does a disservice to us all."

sections.title: Part 3: Terror Suppression
items: South from Crime Alley, at the Malone Improvement District block. It's near a truck to the East.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 504: The rostral anterior cingulate cortex gives us some semblance of control over our fear."

sections.title: Part 4: Hysteria's Song
items: There are two nodes for this part: one on the roof of the East End Free Clinic (image), and the other behind the Free Clinic.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 79: Like Ichabod fleeing the Headless horseman, mediated thought is replaced with a stream of hysteria."

sections.title: Part 5: Pangs of Horror
items: Heroes will find this part inside the first room in the Gotham Sewer, in the dead-end tunnel to the South. A node for this part is also available for all players in the open-world zone, on the building Northwest from East End Free Clinic and South from the Amusement Mile area.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 408: The Toxoplasma gondii parasite will actually suppress the rat's fear, making it actively seek out the scent-marked areas of cats."

Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 81: Adverse reactions to specific stimuli can eventually be removed from the subject via carefully measured exposure."

sections.title: Source overview
items: Assault and control others, either by psychic power or the sheer force of your will. Characters with the mental superpower are masters of mind over matter. Using their unique abilities, they can move objects with a thought to defend themselves or damage an enemy. They can also use the force of their will in more subtle ways, such as creating illusions to disorient and confuse. Mental characters love to be where the action is and control the battlefield with their minds.
Specializing in Crowd Control abilities, Mental is a Power Set available for a character during Character Creation.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Most Celestial Combos require more complex Combos than Light and Rage to activate a power.
Each Celestial Combo can only activate a single power in the opposite tree.
Powers in the Blessed Tree are Golden for both factions.
Powers in the Cursed Tree are Purple for both factions.

The combo version of each power changes to match the first skill used, for instance, a combo starting with a power from the Blessed skill will cause the combo from the Cursed skill tree's power to have the same design, and vice-and-versa, meaning every single skill with a combo in Celestial has 2 kinds of animation, one corrupted and one cleansed.
Similar to Light, the color of weapon attacks change for each faction, being golden for Heroes and dark-purple and black for Villains.
Some Celestial powers are themed after Felix Faust.
Before March 31st, 2015, access to Celestial powers was included in the Sons of Trigon DLC pack. Previous owners of the DLC will retain access to the power.

Some boss encounters in DC Universe Online content utilise Celestial abilities as some of their mechanics. For example, Vampire Lord in the JLD: Darkness Rising operation has several mechanics inspired by various Corrupted abilities that Celestial has.
